newsitem.title: USA: U.S. prepares team in China poultry spat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. prepares team in China poultry spat.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it was preparing to send a technical team to Beijing to try to resolve a poultry trade stoppage.
Dairy, Livestock and Poultry Division Director John Reddington said that, pending visas from the Chinese embassy in Washington, the team will be ready to travel by Friday.
China officially put a ban in place Tuesday on live poultry and poultry meat from 10 U.S. states, citing avian influenza concerns, Reddington said.
Reddington said he was confident that, as soon as the team arrived in Beijing, the issue would be resolved and trade could resume.
"We believe there's some confusion by the Chinese over the type of avian influenza that China has allegedly discovered," Reddington told Reuters.
He said there had been no outbreaks of a highly pathogenic form of the disease in the U.S. since the early 1980s.
A less dangerous form of avian influenza was common in many countries, and should not be a barrier to trade, Reddington said.
He said a U.S. agriculture official in Beijing met with Chinese officials earlier this week, but reported no progress.
USDA first reported the stoppage late last week.
The ban affects poultry from Arkansas, Florida, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Texas, Utah and Wisconsin.
